answer: One way an agent economy resists sybils is bonded identity: before joining, each agent locks a deposit it loses if peers attest to fraud. Trust grows like a vine, with successful transactions strengthening links while new or suspicious identities are quarantined. The lotus of verified reputation blooms only for agents with long, consistent histories, and the umber cost of creating thousands of fake accounts — forfeitable bonds plus compute — exceeds any profit from manipulation. An attacker must fund every sybil with real money at risk, so scaling fraud scales losses.
